requirements.requirement: node1 configured as writable PostgreSQL streaming-replication primary
requirements.summary: postgresql.conf on node1 set wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on, listen_addresses='*'; pg_hba.conf opened replication and client access for the cluster subnet; service started and enabled at boot; replicator REPLICATION LOGIN role created. Confirmed running and accepting writes throughout (INSERTs succeeded on node1 both before and after restart cycle).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via physical streaming replication
requirements.summary: Both nodes were cloned from node1 via pg_basebackup with -R (auto-generated standby.signal + primary_conninfo), attached to dedicated physical replication slots (node2_slot, node3_slot; node3's slot was applied via ALTER SYSTEM + restart after an initial basebackup omitted -S), started, and enabled at boot. pg_is_in_recovery()=t confirmed on both, and pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both client_addrs in 'streaming' state with active slots.
INSERT attempts on node2 and node3 both failed with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction', directly demonstrating standby read-only enforcement.

requirements.requirement: Writes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
requirements.summary: Rows inserted on node1 (repl_test table) were observed identically via SELECT on node2 and node3 immediately after insertion, and again after a fresh write following the full restart cycle of all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol on node2: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 64aad08b... with service healthy and 2 rows visible; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 5aafbe05... (changed, matches fixed after_executor snapshot); service auto-started as standby, pg_is_in_recovery=t, data intact (2 rows), and node1 confirmed it reconnected to streaming.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol on node3: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 3ab2b772... healthy with 2 rows visible; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 0a20ef54... (changed, matches fixed after_executor snapshot); service auto-started as standby, pg_is_in_recovery=t, data intact, node1 confirmed reconnection.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol on node1 (primary): healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered primary role with replication resumed
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 758c051a... with both standbys streaming and 2 rows; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 3669bf4c... (changed, matches fixed after_executor snapshot); service auto-started, both standbys shown streaming again, and a fresh write succeeded and propagated to both standbys.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: node1 is a functioning writable streaming-replication primary, node2 and node3 are correctly configured physical standbys that are read-only and stay in sync with node1, and writes on the primary are directly observed to propagate to both standbys. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and correctly executed and evidenced for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed before/after snapshots and full service/data/cluster recovery demonstrated at each step, including primary role and replication resumption after node1's own restart. Operational hygiene is moderate: an unused SSH keypair/authorized_keys was left configured on all nodes after the executor abandoned SSH in favor of a local nc transfer, two mismatched intermediate pg_basebackup attempts on node2 caused rework (fully corrected, no functional residue), and a few harmless log files were left in /tmp.
limitations: Boot-identity, uptime, and service-state cross-checks rely on captured command output rather than independent verification; no tool access was available to re-inspect the live systems.

The unused SSH authorized_keys/private key residue was not explicitly removed by the executor in the captured trace; absence of a later cleanup command does not rule out one occurring outside the captured window, but none was observed.

Failed-services check was unsupported on this platform (no systemd), so that portion of standard hygiene inventory could not be independently assessed beyond rc-service status checks in the executor trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Core replication build-out was clean and well-verified, but the trace shows several unnecessary or unresolved side effects. (1) Root SSH keypair/authorized_keys were installed on all three nodes (cmd-15ec9c5597454e02, cmd-044083ca3c8546ee, cmd-329be07b35f44789) to enable password-free file transfer, but SSH access was actually blocked by a server-side policy (cmd-e04203329f8a4800, cmd-db04152ac68f4ac9) and the executor fell back to a local nc transfer instead; the SSH keys were never removed, leaving an unused root-login credential path configured on every node — this is residue with mild security relevance that was never cleaned up. (2) A failed python3 http.server attempt (cmd-5589394ea4034735) left /tmp/httpsrv.log on node1. (3) On node2, an initial pg_basebackup without a replication slot (cmd-403e0ddb6d0f4027) was later wiped, and a subsequent attempt using -C -S node2_slot (cmd-d22cf5b5413a4e34) failed because the slot already existed, causing rc-service's auto_setup to accidentally initialize a fresh non-replicated PostgreSQL cluster in its place; this was corrected by a final clean stop/rm/pg_basebackup -R -S node2_slot (cmd-f20b5aa74aa648c7) that produced the correct standby, so no residue remained from these two mismatched attempts but they represent avoidable troubleshooting mutations. (4) /tmp/reboot.log was left on all three nodes as leftover from the reboot-scheduling wrapper. None of these are destructive, security-weakening beyond the unused SSH key, or left the system in a broken state — the final replication topology and package health (apk check) are clean on all nodes per the after_executor snapshot.
